blurb: Shang and Zhou religion — divination, royal ancestors, and the high god Di (later Tian, Heaven) — extended forward through Confucian ethics, Daoist philosophy, state orthodoxy, and modern revival.

events.description: Divination records carved on ox bones and turtle shells at Anyang — the earliest Chinese writing. Shang kings queried ancestors and high gods about harvests, warfare, and ritual.
events.title: Oracle-bone inscriptions

events.description: 305 poems from the early Zhou — folk songs, court odes, and temple hymns including sacrificial odes to royal ancestors. Became one of the Confucian Five Classics.
events.title: Shijing (Classic of Poetry)

events.description: A divination manual of 64 hexagrams with judgments and line statements, built up during the Western Zhou and later expanded into a cosmology of change.
events.title: Yijing (I Ching / Book of Changes)

events.description: Confucius (551–479 BCE) teaches ritual propriety, filial piety, and humane government; sayings of the master and his disciples are gathered over generations into the Analects.
events.title: Confucius & the Analects

events.description: A short, paradoxical classic on the Dao (the Way) and wu wei (action without forcing), attributed to the possibly legendary Laozi; the oldest surviving fragments date to c. 300 BCE.
events.title: Laozi & the Tao Te Ching

events.description: Mencius defends human nature as inherently good and the ruler's duty to the people's welfare, extending Confucius's teaching into systematic political philosophy — and earning a place among the Four Books.
events.title: Mencius & the Confucian school

events.description: Under Emperor Wu of Han, Confucian classics become the basis of state education and official recruitment — a settlement that lasts, with interruptions, into the 20th century.
events.title: Confucianism becomes state orthodoxy

events.description: Zhu Xi fuses Confucian ethics with a metaphysics shaped by centuries of debate with Buddhism and Daoism, and fixes the Four Books as the curriculum of East Asian education.
events.title: Neo-Confucian synthesis — Zhu Xi

events.description: May Fourth reformers attack the Confucian tradition; suppressed again under Mao, Confucian, Daoist, and folk practice revive from the 1980s as temples and festivals return to public life.
events.title: Iconoclasm & revival in modern China

name: Chinese traditions
